title: Claude Code skills: how they work and how to write them
summary: Claude Code skills explained: the SKILL.md format, where skills live, how Claude decides to load one, and three skills to copy, including a pre-PR check.
body_markdown:
Claude Code skills are folders with a` SKILL.md` file: YAML frontmatter that tells Claude when to use the skill, followed by Markdown instructions that Claude follows when it runs. Claude loads a skill on its own when your request matches the skill's description, and you can run any skill yourself by typing` /skill-name` .


Skills are the right home for anything you keep pasting into chat: a checklist, a release procedure, the conventions for one part of the codebase. CLAUDE.md loads in every session, but a skill's body loads only when it's used, so a long procedure costs almost nothing until you need it.


Skill details come from[Anthropic's skills documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) as of October 12, 2026. For the rest of Claude Code (setup, CLAUDE.md, permissions, daily workflow), start with our guide on[how to use Claude Code](https://www.cubic.dev/blog/how-to-use-claude-code) .


## What a Claude Code skill is


A skill is a directory with one required file,` SKILL.md` , plus any supporting files you want Claude to have on hand. The directory name becomes the command, so a skill at` .claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` runs as` /deploy` .


-


Custom commands are now skills. A file at` .claude/commands/deploy.md` and a skill at` .claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` both create` /deploy` . Old command files keep working. Skills add supporting files, control over who can invoke them, and automatic loading.


-


Claude Code skills follow the[Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io/home) open standard. Claude Code adds features on top, such as invocation control, running a skill in a subagent and injecting command output into a skill.


-


Some skills ship with Claude Code. Bundled skills such as` /debug` ,` /loop` and` /claude-api` are prompt-based, and you run them like any skill you write.` /run` and` /verify` launch your app so Claude can check a change against the running app instead of tests alone.

Every frontmatter field is optional, but always write a` description` , because it is what Claude matches your requests against. Claude Code reads frontmatter only when the opening` ---` is the first line of the file. It also ignores field names it doesn't recognize without reporting an error, so a typo such as` disable_model_invocation` silently does nothing.


### Frontmatter fields you will use


Field


What it does


` name`


Command name in the` /` menu. Defaults to the directory name


` description`


What the skill does and when to use it. Claude uses it to decide when to load the skill


` when_to_use`


Extra trigger phrases or example requests, appended to the description


` argument-hint`


Hint shown in autocomplete, such as` \[issue-number\]`


` arguments`


Named positional arguments, used as` $name` in the body


` disable-model-invocation`


` true` stops Claude from loading the skill on its own, so you run it with` /name`


` user-invocable`


` false` hides the skill from the` /` menu, so only Claude can load it


` allowed-tools`


Tools Claude can use without asking during the turn that runs the skill


` model` ,` effort`


Model and effort level while the skill is active


` context` ,` agent`


` context: fork` runs the skill in a subagent, and` agent` picks which type


` paths`


Glob patterns. Claude loads the skill automatically only when it works with matching files


` hooks`


Hooks registered when the skill is invoked, kept for the rest of the session


The[frontmatter reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#frontmatter-reference) lists the rest, including` disallowed-tools` ,` background` and` shell` . If you pin a` model` on a skill, our[ranking of the best LLMs for coding on Bug Bench](https://www.cubic.dev/blog/ai-model-comparison) compares models by the bugs found in their code.


### Arguments and placeholders


Text after the skill name becomes` $ARGUMENTS` , so` /fix-issue 123` turns "Fix GitHub issue $ARGUMENTS" into "Fix GitHub issue 123". You can also take arguments by position with` $0` ,` $1` and so on, or name them in the` arguments` field and write` $issue` or` $branch` . A named argument with no value expands to an empty string.


Skills that ship scripts can use a few variables:` ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` is the skill's own directory,` ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` is the project root, and` ${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}` is the current session ID.


### Injecting live data


` !\`command\`` at the start of a line, or after whitespace, runs the command before Claude sees the skill, and the output replaces the placeholder. For multi-line commands, open a fenced code block with` !` right after the three backticks. This is how a skill can arrive with the current diff already in it.


-


A failing command aborts the whole skill. With the default bash shell, any non-zero exit counts as a failure, except exit code 1 from search and comparison commands, which Claude Code treats as a normal result. Append` || true` to any other command you expect to exit non-zero, such as a check script that exits 1 when it finds problems.


-


Injected commands never prompt for permission. Outside auto mode, a command that your permission rules don't already allow aborts the skill. List the commands in` allowed-tools` to pre-approve them.

## Where skills live


Where you save a skill decides who gets it:


Location


Path


Who gets it


Personal


` ~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`


You, in every project on this machine


Project


` .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`


Everyone in the repo, once you commit it


Nested


` <subdir>/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`


Sessions working in that part of a monorepo


Plugin


` <plugin>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`


Anyone with the plugin enabled, as` /plugin-name:skill-name`


Enterprise


` .claude/skills/` in the managed settings directory


Every user on machines where your organization deploys it


claude.ai account


Skills enabled on claude.ai


Cowork and cloud sessions, and terminal sessions signed in with that account


When two skills share a name, enterprise beats personal and personal beats project. A skill also wins over a` .claude/commands/` file with the same name, and a skill you write replaces a bundled skill of the same name. Plugin skills never collide with yours, because they carry the plugin's prefix.


A few more loading rules:


-


In a monorepo, Claude Code loads project skills from the directory where you start it and from every parent up to the repository root. Skills in a subdirectory below that load the first time Claude reads or edits a file there.


-


Cloud sessions, including Claude Code on the web, don't read` ~/.claude/skills/` on your machine. Commit the skill to the repo's` .claude/skills/` , or enable it on your claude.ai account.


-


Claude Code watches skill directories, so adding, editing or removing a skill takes effect in the current session without a restart. If you create a top-level skills directory mid-session, run` /reload-skills` .


## How Claude decides to load a skill


Claude Code keeps a listing of skill names and descriptions in Claude's context. The full` SKILL.md` stays on disk until the skill is invoked. When your request matches a description, Claude invokes the skill through its Skill tool, and the rendered content enters the conversation as one message.


Two frontmatter fields decide who can trigger a skill:


Frontmatter


You can run it


Claude can run it


In Claude's listing


(default)


Yes


Yes


Name and description


` disable-model-invocation: true`


Yes


Not on its own


Not listed


` user-invocable: false`


No


Yes


Name and description


Whether Claude matches a request to a skill depends on its description, its` paths` and the listing budget:


-


Claude matches against` description` plus` when_to_use` . The combined text is cut at 1,536 characters in the listing, so put the main use case first.


-


With glob patterns set in` paths` , Claude loads the skill automatically only when it works with matching files.


-


The listing gets about 1% of the model's context window. With many skills, Claude Code drops descriptions, starting with the skills you invoke least, and a skill without a description is hard to match. The Skills row in` /context` shows the listing's size, and` /skill-doctor` reports each skill's cost and how often it's used.


Typing the name yourself works differently.` /deploy staging` at the start of a message runs the skill directly. The same name later in a sentence, as in "go ahead and /deploy to staging", only gives Claude permission to run it.


Once loaded, a skill's text stays in the conversation, and Claude Code doesn't re-read the file on later turns. When the conversation is compacted, Claude Code re-attaches the most recent invocation of each skill, but keeps only its first 5,000 tokens, within a 25,000-token budget shared by all skills.


To limit which skills Claude can use, add permission rules.` Skill(deploy)` matches one skill,` Skill(deploy *)` matches it with any arguments, and a deny rule on` Skill` turns skills off.


## How to write a skill that works


Anthropic's troubleshooting notes come back to the same few failures: a description that doesn't match how people ask, a skill that triggers too often, and rules Claude stops following later in a session. These habits prevent most of them:


-


Start from repetition. Turn a prompt you keep pasting, or a CLAUDE.md section that has grown into a procedure, into a skill.


-


Write the description for matching. Lead with what the skill does, then the words people type when they need it, such as "Use when the user asks what changed or wants a commit message." If the skill fires when it shouldn't, make the description narrower.


-


Decide who presses the button. Set` disable-model-invocation: true` on anything with side effects, such as deploys, commits or messages to other people. Set` user-invocable: false` on background knowledge that isn't an action.


-


Keep the body short and direct. Once loaded, every line costs tokens on every turn. Say what to do rather than narrating how or why.


-


Write standing instructions. Claude doesn't re-read the file, so "run the tests after every edit" holds up better than "run the tests".


-


Put the important rules first. After compaction, only the start of a long skill survives.


-


Move detail out. Keep` SKILL.md` under 500 lines and put reference material in linked files.


-


Pre-approve only what the skill needs. The` allowed-tools` grant covers the turn that invokes the skill and clears with your next message. A skill can grant itself broad access, so read the` allowed-tools` of skills checked into a repo before you run Claude Code there.


-


Enforce hard rules with hooks. A skill can't guarantee that a rule holds every time. Claude Code runs a hook every time its event occurs, so a must-hold rule belongs there. Our guide to[Claude Code hooks](https://www.cubic.dev/blog/claude-code-hooks) covers how to write them.


### Test it


A skill that triggers has only been found; it hasn't been shown to help. To check, run a few realistic prompts in a fresh session with the skill on, then again with it set to` "off"` in the` skillOverrides` setting, and compare the results. Anthropic's` skill-creator` plugin automates that loop, including tuning the description, after you run` /plugin install skill-creator@claude-plugins-official` .


When a skill doesn't trigger, ask Claude "What skills are available?" to confirm it loaded. Run` claude plugin validate ~/.claude/skills` (or` .claude/skills` for project skills) to find frontmatter that doesn't parse, or start Claude Code with` --debug` to see the parse error. Broken YAML doesn't stop` /skill-name` from working, but Claude can no longer match the description.


## Three example Claude Code skills to copy


These are examples. Their syntax follows Anthropic's skills docs, but test each one in your own setup before you rely on it. Save each one as` .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` in your repo, or under` ~/.claude/skills/` to use it everywhere. Swap in your own commands and paths.


### 1. A pre-PR checklist


AI-written code needs a check before it goes up for review, like any other code. In the latest full week, Claude Code wrote 78.1% of the AI-written code that cubic reviewed, according to[Bug Bench](https://www.cubic.dev/bugbench/harnesses/claude-code) . That share covers code reviewed by cubic, not the whole market. Inside Claude Code, the model with the lowest relative bug rate is Claude Fable 5.1 at 1.09 (1.00 is average), statistically tied with Claude Sonnet 5.5 at 1.24. Fable 5.1 is ranked on six weeks of data and Sonnet 5.5 on two. Every model ranked there is above that average. A counted bug is a cubic review finding that a developer upvoted or a coding agent addressed.

Why it's built this way:


-


It leaves out` disable-model-invocation` , so Claude can reach for it when you ask "is this ready for a PR?", not only when you remember the command.


-


` allowed-tools` covers the injected git commands. Outside auto mode, an injected command without a matching allow rule aborts the skill.


-


It reports before fixing. You decide what's worth changing, and the list doubles as notes for the PR description.


To run checks on every commit as well, use a skill named` verify` . When a skill named` verify` sits in your personal or project skills at the start of a session, and Claude is allowed to invoke it, Claude Code's commit instructions tell Claude to run it right before each commit, except for changes to docs or tests. This needs Claude Code v2.1.286 or later, and a personal or project skill named` verify` replaces the bundled` /verify` that launches your app. Keep that skill to fast, mechanical checks such as lint, types and tests, and leave the judgment items for the pre-PR pass.


A checklist catches what you already know to look for. It doesn't replace a second reader; see our guide to[AI code review](https://www.cubic.dev/ai-code-review) and[a pre-review safety gate for AI-generated code](https://www.cubic.dev/blog/a-pre-review-safety-gate-for-ai-generated-code) for what comes after it.

The skill uses the GitHub CLI, so` gh` must be installed and signed in.

[cubic's docs](https://docs.cubic.dev/ide/skills) list six skills that cubic publishes for coding agents, including Claude Code:` run-review` ,` check-pr-comments` ,` cubic-loop` ,` codebase-context` ,` review-patterns` and` handle-codebase-scan` .` run-review` , for example, reviews your uncommitted changes or current branch through the cubic CLI, then offers to fix what it finds. ## Share skills with your team


There are three ways to get a skill to other people:


-


Commit it. Project skills in` .claude/skills/` reach everyone who works in the repo, including cloud sessions that clone it.


-


Package it in a plugin. A plugin can carry skills alongside subagents, hooks and MCP servers, with updates from a marketplace. Our guide to[Claude Code plugins](https://www.cubic.dev/blog/claude-code-plugins) covers building and distributing one.


-


Deploy it through managed settings. Enterprise skills reach every user on machines where your organization deploys them.


## FAQ


### What is the difference between Claude Code skills and slash commands?


Custom slash commands have been merged into skills. A file in` .claude/commands/` and a skill in` .claude/skills/` with the same name both create the same` /name` command, and if both exist, the skill wins. Skills add supporting files, invocation control and automatic loading, so use them for anything new.


### How are skills different from CLAUDE.md?


Claude reads CLAUDE.md at the start of every session, so it suits facts Claude always needs, such as build commands, conventions and project layout. A skill's body loads only when it's used. Anthropic's[memory docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory) suggest moving a CLAUDE.md entry into a skill once it becomes a multi-step procedure or only matters for one part of the codebase.


### How do skills relate to subagents?


A skill is a set of instructions, while a subagent runs in its own context window with its own system prompt, tool access and permissions. You can combine them:` context: fork` in a skill's frontmatter runs the skill in a subagent of the type named in` agent` , such as the built-in` Explore` . The subagent doesn't see your conversation, so the skill has to stand on its own.


### Do Claude Code skills work in claude.ai or other tools?


The format follows the Agent Skills open standard, so it carries over. claude.ai uploads and the Skills API accept only six frontmatter fields (` name` ,` description` ,` license` ,` compatibility` ,` metadata` and` allowed-tools` ) and reject the rest, and Claude Code features such as command injection don't work there. Skills you enable on your claude.ai account also sync into Claude Code sessions signed in with that account.


### Do skills use up context?


Every skill Claude can invoke adds its name and description to the context on every turn, and its full body only when it's used. The listing is capped at about 1% of the context window. Run` /skill-doctor` to see each skill's cost and how often it's used, then turn off the ones you don't need.
